hero.sub: A development platform that measures and drives your codebase understanding
hero.h1:
Measure understanding with quizzes and visualize it on an understanding map.
Improve low-quality code with AI-generated fix PRs.
hero.lead:
AI agents leverage sub-agents, MCP, and Hooks to analyze your repository from every angle.
From extracting features and measuring understanding to detecting code quality issues and proposing fixes, everything is automated end to end.
hero.chip1: Advanced repository exploration with AI agents × MCP
hero.chip3: Automatic masking of PII and secrets
challenge.h2: "Understanding debt" is piling up fast in the AI era
challenge.lead: As tools like Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI become widespread, the "development" and "operations" cycle keeps accelerating, but in that rush understanding the code gets pushed aside, and "understanding debt"—the inability to explain what AI-generated code does or why it was written that way—accumulates rapidly.
challenge.c1t: Understanding left behind by "just make it work"
challenge.c1d: Deadlines and deployment speed take priority, and the step of understanding the code is skipped. Work moves forward while no one but the author knows what's inside.
challenge.c2t: Thinking skipped by leaving it to AI
challenge.c2d: Plausible-looking generated code is trusted as-is and shipped to production without ever asking "why is it written this way?" Unexplained code keeps growing.
challenge.c3d: Reviews and tests measure quality, but not people's understanding. There's no telling where to start or how urgent it is.
audience.a1d: Identify where team members' understanding is weak, and prioritize reviews and learning.
audience.a2d: Systematically track where to start understanding, with learning units and quizzes.
flow.h2: Build the resolution of technical debt and understanding debt into your development and operations cycle
flow.sub: End to end, from analysis to measuring understanding, detecting quality issues, and learning and improvement. Repay debt with the twin engines of "measure → learn" and "detect → improve".
flow.s0d: AI agents use MCP to explore the codebase across the board. They cluster files into functional units and grasp the tech stack and dependencies.
flow.s1d: Automatically generate understanding quizzes for each feature. From the answers, objectively measure "who understands what" at the file level.
flow.s2d: Tailored to features that are poorly understood, the agent automatically assembles a learning plan including walkthroughs of the relevant code and technical documentation.
flow.s3d: Analyze duplication, complexity, dead code, traces of AI generation, and more to identify low-quality, high-priority files.
flow.s4d: For low-quality code, AI automatically creates fix PRs. It can also open Issues with assignees.
flow.s5d: With the twin engines of "measure → learn" and "detect → improve", eliminate knowledge silos and continuously improve your codebase's understanding and code quality.
core.c1t: Advanced repository analysis by AI agents
core.c1d: Agents built with Google ADK explore the repository using MCP (Serena / CodeGraphContext / Semgrep / GitHub). They automate generating per-feature learning plans and quizzes, detecting low-quality code, and creating fix plans.
core.c2t: Visualize understanding debt × improve it with quizzes and learning
core.c2d: Cluster source code into functional units and generate a learning plan and understanding check test for each feature. Visualize understanding debt with a graph and actively repay it through the closed loop of quiz → learning.
core.c3t: Recommendations and automatic fixes for low-quality code
core.c3d: For the low-quality code detected during analysis, open recommendations as GitHub Issues. You can assign owners and even automatically create fix PRs.
features.sub: From analysis to dashboards, visualization, and improvement—all in a single workspace.
features.f1t: Dashboard — the big picture at a glance
features.f1lead: Check your repository's understanding and code quality on a single screen.
features.f1li1: ・The matrix organizes files along two axes: "understanding × code quality". Files low on both are the priority areas to improve.
features.f1li2: ・Metrics show understanding, the number of low-quality files, and the number of fixed files, each with its change over time.
features.f1li3: ・The trend graph shows how code quality and understanding change over time.
features.f1li4: ・The priority list lists the files that need attention.
features.f2t: Understanding map — who understands what, and where
features.f2lead: Visualize each user's understanding by feature and file with a graph. Two views are available: map and list. Feature chips let you narrow down to just the files involved in a specific feature. In the map view, nodes = files, lines = dependencies, and color = understanding; selecting a node highlights its adjacent files.
features.f3t: Code quality map — an overview of the quality distribution
features.f3lead: Browse source code file by file and see which files have what room for improvement.
features.f3li1: ・Select a file from the file tree on the left. Files with room for improvement carry a badge.
features.f3li2: ・The contents of the selected file appear on the right. Flagged spots are highlighted so you can check them right there.
features.f4t: Quizzes and learning — measure and deepen understanding
features.f4lead: Take per-feature learning plans and check your understanding with quizzes.
features.f4li1: ・Learning plan list — Check each plan's status and understanding, along with your overall learning progress. Flag units you want to review, and they're gathered at the top of the list.
features.f4li2: ・Open a lesson — Learn repository-specific features through walkthroughs, and refer to the official documentation of related technologies. Understand key processing step by step.
features.f4li3: ・Check your understanding — Take a check quiz. Flag questions you want to review later, and repeatedly review your weak points with retests narrowed to flagged or incorrect answers.
features.f4tag1: ADK agents generate learning plans and quizzes
features.f4tag2: Learn with the twin engines of repository-specific × tech stack
features.f5t: Code improvement — give back via PRs / Issues
features.f5lead: Review improvement points file by file, and automatically generate AI fix Pull Requests or create Issues.
features.f5li1: ・Narrow down with filters and sort by priority. Click an improvement target to open its detail screen.
features.f5li2: ・On the detail screen, the problematic code is highlighted, and you can review the reason for the low quality, priority, and estimated effort.
features.f5li3: ・Choose how to improve: "Have AI automatically create a fix PR" or "Assign an owner and create an Issue".
infra.lead: Using Cloud Tasks, analysis is offloaded to asynchronous workers. Cloud Run auto-scales with load.<br class='hidden sm:block' />New versions are deployed blue-green and rolled out via gradual canary releases, shifting traffic incrementally for zero-downtime, safe switchovers.<br class='hidden sm:block' />Security is ensured with rate limiting via Cloud Armor, plus Secret Manager and Cloud DLP. Infrastructure is codified as IaC with Terraform.<br class='hidden sm:block' />CI/CD runs everything from testing to deployment, plus automatic application of linters/formatters, security scanning, and automated code review by Gemini, keeping code quality high.
security.h2: What we care about in security
security.s1d: GitHub SSO using JWT tokens. Secure session management using access and refresh tokens. Session timeout after 30 minutes of inactivity.
security.s2t: Same-origin delivery and web vulnerability protection
security.s2d: Serving the UI and API from the same origin removes the need for CORS configuration. On top of that, we implement the protections web apps need, such as against XSS, CSRF, and SSRF.
security.s3d: Workload Identity Federation eliminates long-lived credentials. Secrets at deploy time are injected via GitHub Secrets, and at runtime they are consolidated and managed in Secret Manager.
security.s4t: Rate limiting at the edge and within the app
security.s4d: Cloud Armor limits excessive requests before they reach the app. Within the app, administrators can grant and manage credits for repository analysis, preventing abuse of costly analysis processing.
security.s5d: When feeding information to agents, we mask PII and secrets with Cloud DLP (Sensitive Data Protection) and detect-secrets before sending.
security.s6d: We perform OWASP-compliant application vulnerability scanning as well as container image vulnerability scanning using Trivy.
mobile.h2: Check understanding anytime, even on your phone
mobile.sub: With responsive design, you can use the main features as-is from a smartphone.<br class='hidden sm:block' />On the go or between reviews, you can check the understanding map, grasp code quality, and take quizzes.
cta.h2: Make your team's understanding visible, starting today
cta.p: Just connect a GitHub repository and analyze it. You can tackle both understanding debt and technical debt, and slot it right into your daily development and operations (DevOps) cycle.
cta.btn: Connect a repository to get started
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: DevDebtOps (hereinafter the "Service") establishes the following privacy policy (hereinafter this "Policy") regarding the handling of the personal information of users of the Service (hereinafter "users") and the data that users provide.
privacy.1li1: Account information: Your username, email address, public profile, and the like, obtained at login via GitHub integration.
privacy.1li2: Data to be analyzed: The source code and metadata (file structure, commit history, dependencies, etc.) of the GitHub repositories the user connects.
privacy.1li3: Usage data: Quiz answers and learning progress, operation logs, and access logs (IP address, browser information, access date and time, etc.).
privacy.2li1: Providing and operating the Service (measuring understanding, code analysis, generating learning plans and quizzes, proposing code improvements, etc.).
privacy.2li2: Improving the quality of the Service, enhancing features, and addressing defects.
privacy.2li3: Preventing misuse, ensuring security, and analyzing usage.
privacy.3p: The Service integrates with the following external services to provide its features. The handling of information at those destinations follows the rules of each service.
privacy.3li1: GitHub: For authentication and repository integration.
privacy.3li2: AI analysis platforms (Google Vertex AI / Gemini, etc.): For code analysis and learning content generation, we send code and the like to the extent necessary. Before sending, we mask personal information (PII) and secrets.
privacy.4p: Except as required by law or where there is another legitimate reason, we do not provide personal information to third parties without the user's consent.
privacy.5p: When a user uses the Service through an organization they belong to (a team, company, etc.), the administrators of that organization may be able to access members' account settings and data such as analysis results, understanding, and learning status. Handling under organization-level use also follows that organization's policies.
privacy.6p: The information we collect is managed on cloud infrastructure (Google Cloud) after we take appropriate technical and organizational measures such as encryption and access control.
privacy.7p: We retain information for the period necessary to achieve the purposes of use, and after that period elapses or upon a user's request, we appropriately delete or anonymize it. Upon account deletion, the associated data is deleted.
privacy.8p: The Service uses cloud infrastructure (Google Cloud) and AI analysis platforms, and a user's data may be stored and processed on servers outside Japan (such as in the United States). Even in such cases, we take appropriate protective measures in accordance with applicable law.
privacy.9t: 9. Legal bases for processing (for users in the EEA / UK)
privacy.9p: For users in the European Economic Area (EEA) or the UK, we process personal data under the GDPR and similar laws on one of the following legal bases: (1) performance of a contract, (2) compliance with legal obligations, (3) legitimate interests (such as ensuring the safety and improvement of the Service), or (4) the user's consent. Processing based on consent may be withdrawn at any time.
privacy.10p: Users may request disclosure, correction, deletion, suspension of use, and the like regarding their own personal information. When making a request, we may ask you to provide additional information to verify your identity. Depending on the laws of your region (such as the GDPR and CCPA), you may be granted additional rights such as data portability and the right to object to processing. Please contact our support desk.

You can control cookies through your browser settings or DNT / GPC signals, but disabling essential cookies may make some features unavailable.
privacy.12p: This Policy may be revised in response to changes in law or in the content of the Service. In the event of a significant change, we will provide notice on the Service.
